Research interests

My research uses seismology to investigate subsurface structure, surface processes, and changes in the physical properties of geological materials. I combine field deployments of dense nodal arrays with analysis of ambient seismic noise to extract information about seismic sources and the structure through which waves propagate. My approach integrates spatial, temporal, and spectral analysis of continuous waveforms, seismic interferometry to retrieve surface-wave arrivals and scattered coda waves, numerical simulations of wavefield propagation, and development of advanced tomography methods to improve resolution of subsurface heterogeneity. These approaches address questions about connectivity among volcanic magma bodies, sedimentary basin structure, waterfall dynamics and associated seismic signals, and the evolution of material properties during early diagenesis and in response to thermoelastic and tidal strains.
